attachment_requirements_sha256.description: Optional sha256 of the envelope attachment-requirements registry bytes (artifacts/registries/envelope-attachment-requirements.csv) used by the verifier for required-attachment checks.

authentication_status.description: Whether this report verified signer/key identity for the packet. Default verifier runs without a trust keyset and emits HASH_ONLY_NOT_AUTHENTICATED. When --trust-keyset/--auth-keyring is supplied, the bounded Ed25519-JCS-TBS-v1 profile may emit SIGNATURE_VERIFIED or SIGNATURE_FAILED. As of report_version 1.4.0, packet-contained trust keysets are rejected; trust roots must be supplied from outside the packet boundary. As of report_version 1.5.0, callers may require external trust-keyset bytes to match a supplied sha256 pin before SIGNATURE_VERIFIED is possible. This authenticates envelope bytes against the supplied public trust keyset only and does not prove legal authority, online revocation freshness, threshold-policy sufficiency, or live-pilot authorization. As of report_version 1.6.0, trust keysets may also declare a distinct-key-material threshold and reports may expose an external trust-keyset publication receipt status. As of report_version 1.7.0, reports may also expose an optional external trust-governance bundle status that checks synthetic key-ceremony witnesses, key lifecycle events, keyset digest binding, receipt digest binding, and bundle byte pinning. As of report_version 1.8.0, reports may expose an external governance-bundle publication-receipt status. As of report_version 1.10.0, reports may expose an optional external trust-status snapshot gate that checks an explicit verification timestamp, status freshness window, keyset/governance digest binding, status-authority quorum, and trusted-key active/revoked/omitted status. As of report_version 1.11.0, reports may expose an external trust-status-snapshot publication receipt so snapshot bytes are not treated as current merely because they were locally supplied. As of report_version 1.12.0, reports may expose verification-policy lockfile path-scope status so strict policy lockfiles can prove trust-input paths were bounded under a packet-external base directory. As of report_version 1.13.0, reports may expose verification-policy lockfile selector and validity-window status so strict policy lockfiles cannot be replayed against the wrong packet/election/jurisdiction or outside the policy window. As of report_version 1.14.0, strict selector matching requires exact observed packet/election/jurisdiction scope consistency instead of accepting ambiguous mixed-scope packets that merely contain the expected value somewhere. As of report_version 1.15.0, strict verification-policy lockfiles may require external policy-publication receipts and must use caller-supplied verifier temporal context instead of embedding verification_time in policy bytes. As of report_version 1.16.0, verification-policy-lockfile publication receipts may expose temporal validity, policy-issued-at, channel-published-at, and receipt-issued-at ordering checks so policy receipts cannot be replayed outside their receipt window, from future-dated observations, or from evidence that predates the policy it claims to publish. As of report_version 1.16.0, strict verification-policy lockfiles automatically require external policy-publication receipts and fail closed on unknown trust_inputs keys. As of report_version 1.17.0, reports may expose policy-publication-receipt policy-id and packet-selector coherence status so receipts cannot silently describe a different policy or packet scope than the policy bytes being used. As of report_version 1.18.0, trust-status-snapshot publication receipts may expose temporal validity, snapshot-this-update, channel-published-at, and receipt-issued-at ordering checks so revocation/status receipts cannot be replayed from future-dated observations or from evidence that predates the status snapshot it claims to publish. As of report_version 1.19.0, strict authorized reports may expose signer-authorization-roster publication-receipt status and policy-publication-receipt identity/scope coherence status. As of report_version 1.20.0, trust-chain publication-receipt channel entries must carry their own observed digest; channel entries cannot silently inherit the receipt-level digest. As of report_version 1.21.0, strict verification-policy lockfiles may bind to the packet public fingerprint so selector-matching policy bytes cannot be replayed against same-selector different-public-byte packets. As of report_version 1.24.0, strict verification-policy lockfiles and policy-publication receipts may bind the packet-public-fingerprint profile/version as well as the fingerprint digest so future helper-profile changes cannot silently reinterpret old policy bytes. As of report_version 1.25.0, public-fingerprint profile 1.3 preserves warnings for dangling or otherwise unyielded public-surface symlinks so unsafe public routes cannot collapse into ordinary missing-file semantics. As of report_version 1.26.0, public-fingerprint profile 1.4 rejects oversized public files with warnings instead of hashing only prefixes, and also warns on cross-platform reserved public path components such as Windows reserved characters, trailing dots/spaces, and device basenames. As of report_version 1.26.0, public-fingerprint profile 1.4 rejects oversized public files with a warning instead of hashing only a prefix, so strict policy verification cannot be satisfied by a misleading partial public-file digest.
